ai.description: The Sunbeam Snake (Xenopeltis unicolor) reaches 1–1.3m. It has a cylindrical body with iridescent, highly polished scales that flash rainbow colors. Its wedge-shaped head lacks distinct neck constriction.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the highly iridescent, mirror-like sheen of its scales, which appear rainbow-colored even in low light, unlike the duller scales of other snakes.
ai.habitat: The Sunbeam Snake inhabits humid, low-altitude tropical forests, plantations, and rice paddies, often burrowing in loose, moist soil near water sources.
ai.behavior: The sunbeam snake is primarily nocturnal and uses its highly iridescent scales to shimmer with rainbow colors, often burrowing through loose soil to ambush its prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Xenopeltis unicolor* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–17 eggs in soil or decaying vegetation. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sunbeam Snake occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the low-elevation tropical forests of the Brahmaputra Valley and surrounding foothills.
